2_Introduction: The champion device fabricated by perovskite film showed a PCE of 23.8806% with open-circuit voltage (VOC) of 1.1397 V, short current density (JSC) of 25.689 mA/cm², and a fill factor (FF) of 81.564%. The perovskite precursor is Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0. The precursor solution was deposited on the substrate and spin-coated with a two-step spin-coating procedure: 1000 rpm for 5 s and 5500 rpm for 30 s. According to the antisolvent method, 150 µL of antisolvent was dropped on the film 15 s before the end of the program. The substrate was immediately placed on a hotplate and annealed at 110 °C for 15 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The high-performance perovskite solar cell, based on a Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3 composition, leverages the complementary roles of its A-site cations, where the small Cs⁺ ion stabilizes the perovskite lattice, the larger FA⁺ cation expands the bandgap for a higher photovoltage potential, and MA⁺ provides rotational entropy to improve phase stability, collectively optimizing the tolerance factor to suppress ion migration and non-radiative losses. The crystallization dynamics are precisely controlled by the two-step spin-coating procedure (1000 rpm for 5 s, 5500 rpm for 30 s), which establishes a uniform precursor wetting layer followed by rapid solvent evaporation, while the timed introduction of 150 µL of antisolvent 15 seconds before the end of the spin program triggers instantaneous nucleation, yielding a high density of crystallization seeds. Subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 15 minutes then facilitates Ostwald ripening and grain coalescence, effectively healing point defects at grain boundaries and within the bulk, thereby minimizing trap-assisted recombination and enhancing charge carrier lifetimes, which directly translates to improved charge extraction and reduced voltage loss. This optimized film formation process results in a champion device achieving a power conversion efficiency of 23.8806%, with an open-circuit voltage of 1.1397 V, a short-circuit current density of 25.689 mA/cm², and a fill factor of 81.564%.
